key_insight: A small amount of synthetic data helps object detection generalize better, but too much simulation or diffusion-generated data hurts transfer to real-world construction scenes.
engineering_relevance: For data-scarce safety monitoring systems, carefully balancing real and synthetic samples can improve detector robustness without requiring expensive new annotations.
method: Compared Unity simulation rendering and controllable diffusion-based augmentation (CIA) against real-only training.
Used a unified training setup to test multiple real/synthetic mixing ratios under identical model and optimization settings.
Evaluated performance with Precision, Recall, mAP, and custom Δ-metrics across dataset compositions.
evidence_signal: The best result came from 90% real + 10% Unity data with mAP@0.5 = 62.68% (+7.64% over baseline), while Unity-only and CIA-only training reduced mAP@0.5 by about 50% and 16.5%, respectively.
watch_item: Synthetic augmentation is not universally beneficial; excessive replacement of real data can introduce domain drift and reduce real-world transferability.
paper_title: From Unity Simulation to Diffusion-Based Augmentation: Quantifying Dataset Balance for Robust Object Detection
